This game may be a pure combat sandbox for VR at the moment with no campaign structure, so why am I reviewing it when it's not even close to being done yet? I don't typically review early access games.

Because even in it's current form, it is fucking awesome. There is a true dedication to the idea that every physical object is a potential weapon. 

Lost your weapon? Punch a guy in the face and steal his dagger off his hip to stab him with his own dagger.

Need to heal up but don't have enough time to grab another weapon? 
Chug that thing, cork it, and throw the bottle at their face to stun them while you move in for a flurry of martial arts. 

You nimble with your hands? Catch the wrist of a shielded swordsman when they attack you, quickly bend their arm, and smack them in the back of the head and they'll drop their weapon so you can use it against them.

Archer in the distance? YOU CAN CATCH THEIR FUCKING ARROW MID AIR AND START STABBING PEOPLE WITH IT. Don't have the skill to do that? Disarm them by closing the distance and ripping their arrow quiver off their back and smacking them with it. Oh and you have telekinesis so you can send an arrow into someone's face with your mind.

This is one of those rare exception early access games where the base mechanics are so good that the fact that it's not even done yet and is just purely a physics sandbox isn't a mark against it so much as a "Wait, you mean there's gonna be MORE?" Oh yeah, and it's getting mod support implemented in phases, people have already added a glock to the game. Not very blade, but quite sorcery, as I'm casting G U N.

If a combat sandbox of the highest caliber with a high skill ceiling, VR or otherwise, interests you, and you have a VR headset, you owe it to yourself to get this. You can do some high caliber, recording worthy shit in this game and I love it.

[h1]Don't play this in a serious manner![/h1]

This game is great for feeling like a psycho ripping people apart mid air or stabbing people 32 times before tossing them off a cliff but any serious sword fighting doesn't really work. 

[h1]The sword fighting[/h1]

Holding a sword in VR doesn't let you feel the weight of what the object actually has, so swinging it feels kinda wrong. It works once you pretend the object has the weight you think it has (or just useing the rapier) but it then ends up feeling too weak. 

[h1]AI needs something different[/h1]

The AI feels .. stupid. They walk up to you, attack and dodge depending what difficulty they are. They have a strict animation set to their attacks, and they work if they only come a bit closer, but especially during their more difficult movesets, they just walk into you, making you give them a hug with your sword, and having to free yourself and the sword from behind their back absolutely destroying immersion.

 [h1]Controller destruction simulator[/h1]

You can't really blame this on the game to be honest. Of course someone with a 6x6 meter playspace will have no problems with this. [h1]🟩Pros[/h1]
+Accurate Melee Combat, the best in VR yet
+Sandbox Nature
+Modding Community

[h1]🟥Cons[/h1]
-No campaign or career mode yet
-Little to no “Sorcery” yet
-AI has room for improvement

[h1]🎮Gameplay Analysis[/h1]
When it comes to VR gaming, nothing comes close to the accuracy and realistic depiction of the melee combat of Blade and Sorcery. It’s a sandbox game (for now) that allows you to pick from a wide selection of weapons ranging from axes, spears, and swords to bows and arrows. Use them on different spawnable enemies like swordsmen, mages, and archers across 4 different arena type maps. With the possibility to add more content through mods.

[h1]🗡️Setting the bar in Blade[/h1]
Blade and Sorcery definitely sets the bar high for VR melee combat, to the point that it’s hard to enjoy other VR melee games anymore. The game offers 1:1 replication of movement without the use of any gestures and animations whatsoever. The only thing different from your movement is that it compensates weapon weight by adding delays to your movement; the heavier the weapon, the higher the delay, and it works pretty well. You can swing, thrust, stab, parry, deflect and even throw your weapons to inflict damage to opponents. There is also dismemberment and gore to add to the realism. It uses a full physics engine for every object, meaning every item or npc is movable and interactive at all times.

[h1]🔥What about the Sorcery?[/h1]
While Blade and Sorcery got the Blade aspect right, the Sorcery part is still lacking. There is only one spell in the game: Lightning that functions very similarly to the force lightning in Star Wars, inflicting damage and limiting their movement. Aside from that, you can lift objects, push or pull them to you using telekinesis like the force but it’s more of a quality of life tool to pick objects up easily. You can also slow down time like Max Payne and it adds an awesome layer to the already fun melee combat, simulating superhuman reflexes without actually having any. It isn’t much though considering this is 50% of the name of the game, but the dev has plans to amp it up next few patches.

[h1]🕹️Sandbox Singleplayer in early access[/h1]
The game is entirely sandbox and in singleplayer. Meaning no missions, campaigns, career, story or progression system in place. Not even a gladiator career mode style of campaign. Having said that, the lone developer definitely has plans to add them in the future and you can already see the foundation to cater the aforementioned features in the game. Right now you can just select a map to play, and spawn enemies in a bunch of different ways and difficulties, trying out many different weapons; literally sandbox gameplay.

[h1]🧀Cheese your way to victory[/h1]
Taking into account that this is a VR melee combat game with 6DoF movement, the AI is actually decent. It can block your attacks from all directions and defend itself relatively well. But when you really want to just win and ignore the roleplaying feel of the game, you can easily wiggle and flap your swords around to victory. This works best with dual wielding cause enemies can’t defend against dual attacks. The AI only has like 5 animations for attacks and that’s it. They can pretty much telegraph their attacks and it can get repetitive. I would love to see more dynamic attacks from AI and combos at that. They also don’t have sword/weapon locking in place. Now I don’t know if they really have those in real life as opposed to the movies but it would be a cool addition.

[h1]🛠️Modding is a game changer, literally[/h1]
For a niche offline game that requires niche hardware, you’d expect zero to little modding support. But not Blade and Sorcery; the modding community is great and active, providing mods such as additional weapon packs, maps, even overtaking the developer by adding their own ‘campaign’ like maps or even working guns. My favorite is the Star Wars mod that actually gives you lightsabers, blasters, and some maps. It’s so well made that it doesn’t feel like a mod and instead feels like a proper Star Wars game! and you should see it for yourself down below.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OtqYz63rK-o 

[h1]🖥️Technical Analysis[/h1]
The game works flawlessly with my Oculus Quest headset using the official Oculus Link. Even better with the unofficial ALVR untethered app, because I can play wirelessly anywhere in my house that has a 5GHz signal which is basically everywhere.

Regarding the VR mechanics, the game only allows the use of locomotion movement either directed by the controller or your headset. I’m fine with this because it’s a melee fighting game. It also allows for various VR options within the game like height adjustment, snap turning, and hand reach adjustment.

Performance is very smooth for my i7-8700k and GTX 1080. I even increased the rendering resolution a bit to make it look more crisp. As far as VR visuals go, it isn’t the best I’ve seen, but passable enough to enjoy a realistic melee combat experience.

[h1]💸Value and Conclusion[/h1]
Blade and Sorcery is a must have for any VR headset owners out there. Both as a ‘showcase’ game to friends and family and as a ‘go to’ game whenever you need that realistic melee combat fix. It is no doubt worth the price of admission, sale or not. Even if it’s still early access it blows many VR games out of the water and will only get better.

What makes B&S so good with melee is how much depth the melee combat has. You truly have to think in 3 dimensions to play well. Hitting an enemy in the legs or arms does less damage and in the head does more. You have to get around the enemies sword and shield to hit them. You have to maintain distance and understand the length of your weapon. Each weapon has vastly different strengths and weaknesses and how you use them really matters.

On top of that, there's a quality that B&S has that other VR melee games don't seem to understand. The hits you pull off in this game are incredibly rewarding because enemies can actually die in one hit, and even if they don't, the hits feel damaging. This game has thrown out a lot of the numbers based RPG style combat of the fantasy themed games that inspire it and instead, stronger, better geared enemies don't require better weapons to kill them, but rather, only more skill.

The big fat cherry on top is that basically any problem you have with this game can be modded, and it's incredibly easy to do so yourself or just find mods other people have made.

While this game is mostly yet another VR arena sandbox (the best one), that is changing with coming updates and within a few years of this review it will have a fully fleshed out procedural dungeon game mode with progression. This game has been the gift that keeps on giving for years since I got it and if you have VR it's simply a must try unless you are violence averse or something.

I'm a bit torn with blade and sorcery, whilst it is fun and the best VR game of its type I have played, I also think that they took it in a direction I am personally not to keen on or interested in.

I much would of preferred development to focus on smaller objectives like storming a fort of enemies, maybe even with some AI allies rather then an attempt at dungeons. With more focus on enemy animations and making the combat better. Some actual challenging enemies, not in terms of stats, but in how they fight, with correct use weapons, perhaps even enemies that work together as a shield wall even.

I was never really keen on the whole magic thing either and some of the new enemies are a bit confusing to me: I always thought the climbing kinda sucked in this game.

I can see what they are going for and I like this game its fun, but I also feel also a little disappointed with it, like it is not reaching its potential.

Edit: I can say after playing longer that the flaws of this game became very overt, to the point I could no longer enjoy the game. 
I can kill most enemies by waiting for them to impale themselves on my weapon. 
I've never seen them block with a weapon. 
They have a 'dodge' animation where they jump backwards, but it always plays after you've attacked, making it useless.
You can't block sometimes due to your hitbox being janky, you may as well always attack.
Hard to use any long weapon like a spear as your hands won't be in the 'correct' spot, but also due to the fact you can't bend your wrists in game, you can't stab downwards with a spear while keeping your left hand upwards in game, but obviously you can in reality.
The damage of weapons is very unbalanced and unrealistic, warhammer is easy mode and kills everything in one hit, powerattack/downwards cut with sword often leaves a scratch, same attack might randomly take a limb off. Not consistent.
Numerously AI behaviours that leave me scratching my head, for instance a disarmed enemy will ALWAYS run at and past you, the only reason this sometimes works is because you have a camera on your face and you can't hit stuff directly infront of you without hitting your VR set, otherwise they just impale themselves as usual. This can be very fustrating if kind of funny if using any kind of stabbing weapon against plate armor, as they will just keep running past you whilst doing nothing.
Weapons often getting stuck inside enemies, no not as you would expect, stuck as in you can lift the enemy off the ground with a spear vertically stuck.
The enemies like to run circles around you at times, which can be annoying if you are trying to align yourself to avoid the obstacles in your room, would be nice to have optional setting to have them more aggressive at the 'front' of the player for duels at least.
And lastly, my personal gripe, hands not staying in the position you gripped your weapon. This is extremely annoying with weapons like the longsword where after stabs you often find both hands gripped the top of the sword handle for some reason.

There's more but you get the picture, fun but flawed game that will only entertain you so long.

blade and sorcery advertises itself as a VR melee & magic fighting game but honestly a more accurate description would be "VR fantasy physics sandbox".
sure you can swordfight and spell cast, pick up a spear or a hammer, whatever, but you can also just as easily use telekinetic power to pick up a nearby barrel and bash your adversary in the back of their big, stupid unsuspecting head.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3255821785

want to ditch the weapons altogether and get your hands bloody? you can absolutely do that. your fists are just as powerful as anything else with enough force, and the enemies are grabbable from multiple different points on their body. (can't headbutt tho)

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3255851703

enemies themselves are a little underwhelming, big meat sacks with canned animations and cold, expressionless stares, limited to one-handed weapons and dual wielding. if you punish them hard enough they either fall over (great opportunity for a finisher) or die. a few different classes with some unique abilities. they can do just about everything you can besides kick, grab, or jump. i don't know if they're fun to FIGHT, per se, but they are fun to torture, so they serve their purpose well enough.

let's say you want to ditch the fighting as well.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3255824863 

that's ok. like i said this is a physics sandbox game. everything behaves at least mostly how you'd expect it to, so theres plenty of fun to be had in experimenting.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3255837805


the maps are decently sized, have plenty of props, and unique areas, and are very traversable. see somewhere, you can probably go it. although, if you can't see it, you likely CAN'T go there. there are invisible walls. i can tell you right now that almost all doors you see are unopenable. BUT i can't say the same for kill barriers. from my experience the maps have no kill barriers, only damage will do you in.
misjudge the distance of a jump and fall into the canyon map's... well... canyon?

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3255810056

it's not the end for you. aim your fall into the river that runs through it, then find dry land, and use the bricks of the bridge to climb your ass back up there, because the game has a climbing detection system.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3255812691 

granted, it's a little finicky, but if you really get tired of the trial and error of finding edges to grab on, you can turn on an option that lets you climb anything. see if you can descend a mountain without killing yourself, it's an interesting challenge.

the version of the game you see youtubers playing probably isnt the exact same game because the modding community is (somewhat) healthy. nexus mods (and the other one i won't name, i GUESS) hosts plenty. creators i would recommend checking out are HuJohner for various quality of life and just overall cool mods, Mxthic and Fable005 for a wider variety of maps, and I would also recommend looking on youtube for various mod reviewers who will probably give you a list of the "essential" ones they use to max their fun.

Overall rating: 10/10. One of the best VR games I have ever played, with a clear amount of love from the developers and community alike. It is worth far more than the asking price of [strike]$20[/strike] $30 USD. You can see how much I love this game from my play time alone.

Good Things About this Game:

1. Swordplay is fun and satisfying.
2. Best two-handed melee weapon handling I have seen in a VR game as of yet.
3. There is a focus mechanic that lets you do cool things in slow motion.
4. It is made of a relatively small group of developers who clearly love the game.
5. Tired of fighting in arenas? There is a whole randomly generated dungeon you can run through and slaughter all of your enemies.
6. One of only a few combat-based VR games where stealth is also an option.
7. A good amount of weapon variety with shortswords, longswords, handaxes, greataxes, daggers, staves,  maces, war hammers, spears, bows and arrows, a rapier, a dual bladed staff, and wrist blades so we can pretend the developers of Assassin's Creed Nexus care about Vive and Index users.
8. Great world building through notes you can find throughout the dungeons.
9. Many beautiful locations to cover with the blood and severed limbs of your enemies.
10. A fully fledged skill tree.
11. One NPC.

Good Things that are also Spoilers:
1. [spoiler] Hector, a giant golem you fight at the end of the Dalgarian dungeons is very fun to fight.[/spoiler].
2. [spoiler] Fun skills, such as the ability to force choke people, shoot homing arrows, and literally rip your enemies limb from limb with your bare hands.[/spoiler].
3. [spoiler] A cool story where I didn't bother to decipher any of the notes and so I stumbled right into the bad ending.[/spoiler].
4. [spoiler] There is a secret good ending.[/spoiler].
5. [spoiler] Two of the factions are hell-bent on the wholesale slaughter of innocent people so you don't have to feel bad for creeping up behind them and shoving them off of the nearest ledge.[/spoiler].
6. [spoiler] The Eye, with their advanced magic and tough armor are fun to fight against[/spoiler].
7. [spoiler] The end of the game is a full and complete power fantasy. [/spoiler].

Bad Things About this Game:

1. Weapons can only be effectively gripped by the handle, which somewhat limits how you fight.
2. You can't reliably fight against enemies with a certain type of weapon. i.e., if you want to fight an enemy with a rapier, you have to either kill enemies until one with a rapier spawns, or disarm them, throw a rapier on the ground far enough from you that they will maybe pick it up, and hope that they pick it up instead of heading straight for the door.
3. The new Vive screenshot key doesn't work so you have to use F12, which can be tricky in VR.
4. [spoiler] The big door at the player's home base seems like it would lead to a boss battle but it just leads directly to the ending of the game, which kind of feels anticlimactic, but it still makes for a satisfying ending.[/spoiler].
5. [spoiler] There are no restored variants of the early-game weapons (the seax, warbrand, and cleaver), so if you want to use them, you have to use the old rusty ones. [/spoiler]
6. [spoiler] If you lose the Sword of Naa, it doesn't go to your stash. [/spoiler].
7. There are a few bugs that can destroy permadeath playthroughs. Ex. Second wind doesn't work with Hector, there are a few walls you can get trapped in, etc.

Needless to say, I love this game and have no small amount of respect for the developers and community as a whole.

Absolutely yes. If you own a VR headset, this game is mandatory. Good modding scene and is actively being worked on by the devs. This isn't a story game however, it's more so a sandbox where you test your skills and experiment as much as you want. Very recently, however, an update was released that added a more "objective-oriented" (for lack of a better term) map which is procedurally generated and introduced stealth mechanics. This game is good for anyone who likes consistent action, more so than someone who wants to complete a physics puzzle (just play Boneworks at that point) or have long, calm periods of time between battles (just play Boneworks at that point).

First, this game should come with a hazard warning. I've already broken a controller thank fck and had myself nearly smashed into my kitchen wall playing this. It's that immersive and adrenaline pumping. I've actually decided not to play this game until I can expand my play area because otherwise there won't be anything unbroken in my room before long.

Second, be prepared to face the hidden devil in you, because this game will bring out the worst of you. I don't care if you are a little white bunny or a fluffy little kitten, this game will turn you into a blood-thirst mindless man-slaughtering monster. That feeling of grabbing someone's head and stabbing his chest with a dagger in your hand or cutting someone's leg right off with one single sword slash is ... disturbingly satisfying. When you are in that setting, you just couldn't help but enjoy killing people and hearing the sound of your sword piercing their body and the blood bursting out. There's something about it. Maybe it activates the reptilian part of your brain or something.

The game is pretty bare-bones at the moment (even after a year and a half in EA), with 4 'sandbox' maps where you can fight waves after waves of AI enemies using different weapons (and one spell). That's it. Zero story, quest, progression. Nothing. So, don't expect anything beyond a basic VR gladiator simulation for now.

For future development, I would suggest adding sex, drugs, alcohol and gambling into this game, and making it the best all-round debauchery simulator with a bit of RPG elements and a light storyline. Just imagine that: You are a gladiator in Rome or a medieval mercenary, having just slain your enemies in an epic battle with their blood fresh on your hands, and then get drunk at the local tavern and have a blast with a wench of your choosing. Oh yeah, give me some of that.

Still a fun game in its current shape though. I doubt you would get very many hours from it, but it's worth the price just for the VR combat experience.

1. The campaign has "procedurally generated" dungeons which is a fancy way of saying about a dozen rooms randomly rearranged. I still liked it though. However I didn't finish it. I killed the boss twice and I had seen enough. 
2. The game does not require very quick reflexes, which is a good thing because VR tracking is not that good enough to simulate the speed of a real sword fight. I am using Oculus Quest 2 on Air Link and I frequently found myself switching to slowmo to prevent desyncs. Maybe more expensive headsets are better. 
3. The campaign added quite a bit of parkour, which made me rage, swear and sweat a lot. 
4. Me and many others on the internet randomly get boners while playing the game apparently. 
5. I am getting some weird lag spikes when I load into high poly sections large levels and it desyncs my left and right eyes. Turning the headset off and on again fixes that. It happens a lot, sometimes even mid fight. 

Don't let the June 2024 release date fool you. This game is almost as old as VR itself. One of the top 5 VR games of all time easily IMO.
